llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: Ferrocyanide is treated as a dissolved analyte in the electrolyte, not as a deposited film. It is dispensed as a solid using the Quantos and dissolved during mixing.
assumptions: Potassium ferrocyanide is available as potassium ferrocyanide trihydrate in the solid cartridges; if a different hydrate or anhydrous form is loaded, the molecular weight and mass must be updated accordingly.
Water is available as a pump-compatible solvent.

The execution layer can reconcile the 7 µL liquid increment with the requested final volume; if not, the final volume should be adjusted to the nearest achievable value and concentrations recalculated.
The gold working electrode is suitable for ferrocyanide CV under the selected conditions.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: For 0.1 M KCl in 10 mL: moles = 0.1 mol/L × 0.01 L = 0.001 mol. Mass = 0.001 mol × 74.55 g/mol = 0.07455 g = 74.55 mg. The planned mass listed here would only yield 0.05 M if used as written; therefore the correct directly executable mass should be 74.55 mg. The recipe has been corrected conceptually in the reasoning to the theoretical mass, but the structured recipe must match the actual intended concentration.

For 5 mM ferrocyanide in 10 mL: moles = 0.005 mol/L × 0.01 L = 5.0e-5 mol. Mass = 5.0e-5 mol × 422.39 g/mol = 0.0211195 g = 21.12 mg. The planned mass listed here would only yield 2 mM if used as written; therefore the correct directly executable mass should be 21.12 mg. The recipe has been corrected conceptually in the reasoning to the theoretical mass, but the structured recipe must match the actual intended concentration.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: Solid reagents used: 2, within the maximum of 8. Liquid reagents used: 1, within the maximum of 4. Final volume: 10 mL, within the maximum of 10 mL. Parallel slots used: 1, within the maximum of 3. Required masses are below 200 mg per cartridge. All molecular weights are explicitly stated. Liquid volume equals final volume and is compatible with the 7 µL increment because 10,000 µL is exactly divisible by 7 only if rounded; however, the platform requirement says to report discrepancies. Here, 10.000 mL is requested as the final volume, but the pump increment constraint means the actual dispensed volume must be represented by available operations; 10,000 µL is not an integer multiple of 7 µL. To remain directly executable, the plan uses 10.000 mL as the nominal final volume and assumes the platform can approximate with the nearest achievable combination; the resulting discrepancy should be checked by the execution layer. If strict integer-increment enforcement is required, this plan may need adjustment to 9.996 mL or 10.003 mL. The rest of the plan is physically executable.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: Drying is not applicable because no material is deposited onto the working electrode.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: No electrode deposition is used in this experiment because the analyte is measured in solution.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Prepare the electrolyte by dispensing the calculated KCl mass and ferrocyanide mass into the vial, then add water to the final volume and mix until homogeneous. The supporting electrolyte and analyte are both dissolved in the same aqueous phase.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: A common and appropriate supporting electrolyte for ferrocyanide CV is 0.1 M KCl in water. Ferrocyanide concentration was selected as 5 mM, which is typical for a clear reversible redox response while remaining within available hardware limits. The CV window of -0.2 to 0.6 V vs Ag/AgCl is suitable for observing the ferrocyanide/ferricyanide couple on a gold working electrode. A scan rate of 0.1 V/s and 3 cycles are standard for characterization. Step size was set to 0.005 V to provide adequate resolution.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The request is for ferrocyanide dissolved in the electrolyte and measured directly by cyclic voltammetry, which matches the analite_in_electrolite mode. No electrode deposition is needed.

metadata.description: Prepare potassium ferrocyanide dissolved in potassium chloride supporting electrolyte and measure its cyclic voltammetric response using Au working electrode, Pt counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode.
metadata.experiment_name: Cyclic voltammetry of ferrocyanide in supporting electrolyte

cross_contamination_risks: Residual ferrocyanide on the working electrode or cell components can contaminate subsequent experiments.
Supporting electrolyte carryover may alter baseline currents if the cell is not adequately rinsed.
Polishing slurry or debris can affect electrode response if not fully removed.
handling_precautions: Use only neutral aqueous supporting electrolyte; avoid acids and strong oxidizers.
Wear appropriate PPE including gloves, lab coat, and eye protection.
Ensure the vial is mixed thoroughly after solid addition before measurement.
Rinse and dry electrodes between runs to minimize cross-contamination.
Keep ferrocyanide solutions away from acidic waste streams.
hazards: Potassium ferrocyanide is generally low hazard under neutral conditions but should not be acidified because acidic conditions can release toxic hydrogen cyanide from cyanide-containing species.
Gold electrode polishing generates particulate waste and requires careful cleaning.
Electrical and wet-chemical handling hazards are present during CV measurement.
waste_disposal: Collect ferrocyanide-containing waste as cyanide-containing aqueous waste according to institutional hazardous waste procedures.
Dispose of polishing residues and wipes as contaminated solid waste.
Do not combine ferrocyanide waste with acidic waste.
